granite crushers exposed to silica concentrations about twice the present threshold limit value (TLVs) have a greater decrease in forced expiratory volume, forced expiratory flow and compliance of the lungs than matched referents.

the granite crushers had, on average, small but significant changes in pulmonary function after 12 years of exposure to silica dust at a concentration about twice the TLV.

the granite crushers had a small, but significant, deterioration of their lung function over 12 years, and that the granite workers had more pronounced functional changes than the referents, especially in smokers.
the risk of developing silicosis in the granite industry seems to be low, but that a small but significant risk of developing airways obstruction is present, especially in tobacco smokers.
